html: Descaling on the EP2230/14: Philips groups this model with the 0800/1200/2200/3200 button-control series. When Calc/Clean calls for a cycle, remove LatteGo and the AquaClean filter, use the specified Philips descaler and a 1.5 L catch container, then hold Calc/Clean for three seconds and start the cycle. The separate fresh-water rinse must finish before a new AquaClean filter is installed and activated. Philips says not to interrupt descaling; it can take up to 30 minutes. A used 2200 therefore needs both the filter history and a demonstrated completed cleaning cycle, not merely a seller's claim that a filter is fitted. Checked October 17, 2026. [source]
note: Philips lists EP2230/14 and gives the 0800/1200/2200/3200 button sequence, filter removal, 1.5 L vessel, rinse and reactivation.

html: Refurbishment check for EP4347/94: Philips puts the 4300 descaling cycle in the screen's Clean > Descaling menu. The owner removes LatteGo and the AquaClean filter, empties the tray and grounds bin, uses Philips descaler with a 1.5 L container, and completes both the guided descale and rinse before installing and activating a new filter. Philips describes about 30 minutes for this family. That is a useful handover test for a refurbished unit: ask whether the seller completed the guided cycle and whether the filter counter was restarted, instead of treating a newly fitted filter as proof of prior care. Checked October 17, 2026. [source]
note: Philips lists EP4347/94 and gives the 4300/4400/5400/5500 menu sequence, filter removal, 1.5 L vessel and new-filter activation.

html: Care cost behind the 12-drink menu: EP5447/94 follows Philips' 4300/5400 screen-guided Clean > Descaling route. The milk unit and AquaClean filter come off, the tray and grounds bin are emptied, and a 1.5 L vessel catches the descaler and rinse over roughly 30 minutes; a new filter is installed and activated only after completion. If evaluating a used four-profile 5400, test that the Clean menu and prompts work and request its filter and descale history. Four saved recipes do not reduce this shared water-path maintenance. Checked October 17, 2026. [source]
note: Philips lists EP5447/94 and documents screen-guided descaling, milk/filter removal, 1.5 L vessel, about 30 minutes and reactivation.

html: Dial and dose boundary: Baratza assigns settings 1–20 to its finer espresso adjustment range and 21–40 to filter and coarser methods. The Encore ESP starts by a pulse button or on/off knob and lists manual dosing; its included 54 mm cup has a 58 mm adapter. Record the actual setting and grounds weight when changing brew methods rather than treating a dial number as a weighed dose. The product page also says shims can move the fine range, so a used unit's setting numbers may not match a factory setup. Confirm the supplied cup, adapter and shim state before using another owner's recipe. Checked October 17, 2026. [source]
note: Official US ZCG495 page specifies 1–20 espresso, 21–40 filter, manual dosing, cup/adapter and shim-adjustable fine range.

html: Second-generation setup check: Fellow's Opus 2 change record confirms a single stepless dial, 48 mm burrs, revised grounds path, magnetic brush and automatic stop with jam alert. On a used or mixed-stock listing, verify those features and the exact Opus 2 label before applying this review. The first-generation Opus has different controls. Checked October 17, 2026. [source]
note: Fellow's September 30 Opus 2 change record distinguishes the redesigned path, 48 mm burrs, brush, stepless adjustment and jam alert from original Opus.
